newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH CSU SURVEY SEES Q1 CZK 45 BLN TRADE GAP.
newsitem.headline: CZECH CSU SURVEY SEES Q1 CZK 45 BLN TRADE GAP.

text.p: The Czech Republic's trade deficit for the first quarter of 1997 should nearly double, year-on-year, to 45 billion crowns, a survey of importers and exporters by the Czech Statistical Bureau (CSU) showed on Wednesday.
The trade balance for the first quarter of 1996 stood at a 27.1 billion crown deficit, while the first quarter 1995 trade gap was 17.5 billion crowns.
The CSU said in a statement that the survey included estimates from firms which accounted for 20 percent of all import business last year, and 36 percent of exports.
The CSU said 170 firms were polled in the survey, of which 67 percent responded.

The survey showed that total imports are expected to rise in the first quarter by some 10 percent, year-on-year, with raw materials, foodstuffs and machinery imports accounting for most of the growth.
Total imports in the first quarter of 1996 were 174.3 billion crowns.
Import prices are expected to edge about two percent higher overall, though prices of chemicals and related products, beverages and tobacco should ease slightly.
It added that total exports for the quarter should remain static at last year's 147.2 billion crown level. Export prices should rise by about 2.5 percent, year-on-year.
The CSU itself has issued a the Czech Republic's overall 1997 trade deficit to rise to between 211-219 billion crowns after last year's record shortfall of 160.3 billion crowns.
The bureau has not issued its own quarterly estimate.
Analysts say the first quarter is usually a slow period for importing and exporting in the Czech Republic, and expect both sides to grow substantially in the second quarter.
